evidence: Read the staged shell MyAccessibilityService.kt and all ten collaborator files under a11y, eval, model, parser, picap and whatsapp, then compared the index against both parents with git diff HEAD and git diff 43ab360 to see which side each file came from; all four result files and the build evidence were then rewritten as a single set describing this merge tree.
Grepped the kilometre extraction regex, the picapWindows identifier, pendingCloseId, hasScannedInitially and every import in the new modules to check for dead code, shadowing and duplicated helpers.

Compared blob hashes and line counts of the gentle-review artifacts across base accf641, HEAD b661327, the other parent 43ab360 and the index to determine whether the merged set describes one tree; the stale mixed-lineage artifacts have been replaced by this review's results.

findings.claim: Both collaborators receive a window supplier named picapWindows and immediately declare a local val of the same name by invoking it, so for the rest of the function the reader must decide whether picapWindows means the provider or the list. The shell already names the identical lambda picapWindowsProvider and the KDoc calls the parameter a provider, so the injected name is the odd one out. Pre-existing at 43ab360.
proof_refs: PicapOfferProcessor line 22 declares private val picapWindows of function type and line 40 assigns a local picapWindows by invoking it, after which lines 41 to 94 only ever mean the list.

PicapOfferCloser line 35 declares the same function-typed parameter and its KDoc at line 28 documents it as provider of the Picap window roots, yet attemptNonCvClose line 86 shadows it with a local list of the same name.
MyAccessibilityService line 51 names the same lambda picapWindowsProvider and the identical declarations exist unchanged at revision 43ab360.

findings.claim: The same kilometre extraction regex for the same origen field is written twice, once as a private helper in WhatsAppResponder and once inline in NotificationInterceptorService, even though the whole point of routing both paths through evaluateAutoAccept was to share that logic. The eval package now owns the threshold comparison for both callers but not the parsing that produces the km argument, so a fix to one copy will not reach the other. Pre-existing at accf641 and 43ab360.
proof_refs: WhatsAppResponder line 176 builds a regex matching digits followed by km inside private fun extractKmFromWhatsApp, while NotificationInterceptorService line 159 builds the identical regex inline on service.origen.
Both call sites construct AutoAcceptConfig and call evaluateAutoAccept imported from the eval package, so the shared piece is the comparison but not the extraction feeding it.
The same pair exists at accf641 where the helper lived in MyAccessibilityService and at 43ab360 where it had already moved to WhatsAppResponder.

findings.location: picap/PicapOfferCloser.kt:41 pendingCloseId and picap/PicapListAutoclicker.kt:17 hasScannedInitially, written from picap/PicapOfferProcessor.kt:54 and :128-131
findings.claim: Both fields were private in the base monolith and are now internal mutable state owned by one class but written by another, yet neither declaration carries a KDoc naming the external writer or the write sequence. The comments at the declarations still describe only single-class behaviour, so the cross-class protocol is left to be inferred from the call site. Pre-existing at 43ab360.
proof_refs: PicapOfferCloser line 41 declares a volatile internal var whose preceding comment speaks of writing in the event and releasing in the coroutine without naming PicapOfferProcessor as the writer.

PicapListAutoclicker line 17 declares internal var hasScannedInitially with only the comment about the initial list scan, while PicapOfferProcessor line 54 assigns it back to false after a captured order.
The identical declarations and comments exist unchanged at revision 43ab360, and the base revision had both fields private inside the single monolith file.
